newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Pyongyang said making new business pitch to Seoul.
newsitem.headline: Pyongyang said making new business pitch to Seoul.

text.p: Pyongyang is apparently seeking to mend fences after South Korea boycotted an investment forum in its free-trade zone, media reports said on Tuesday.
It has invited a Seoul delegation for an exclusive look at the capitalist-style zone along the Tumen river near China and Russia, newspapers and state media said.

In a letter to South Korea's Foreign Minister Gong Ro-myung, the Hong Kong office of North Korea's Committee for the Promotion of External Economic Cooperation invited 150 South Koreans to a four-day forum in Rajin-Sonbong.
South Korea withdrew its delegation from an international investment fair in Rajin-Sonbong from September 13 to 15 after Pyongyang refused to accept its officials and journalists.
Pyongyang issued invitation letters to 25 South Korean business representatives, turning down 28 applicants.
It argued it lacked accommodation for the South Korean delegation, but nevertheless invited officials from China, Japan and the United States.
The latest offer made clear officials and reporters would be welcome, the media reports said.
A Foreign Ministry official confirmed a letter had been received, but declined to give further details.
"We need to make clear whether this was an official offer from the North. We will unveil our stance over the letter soon," the official said.

Desperate for foreign cash to ease its food crisis, Pyongyang made its boldest ever pitch to foreign business executives last week in its Rajin-Sonbong free trade zone, the only foreign investment window of its kind in North Korea.
On Monday the official North Korean media trumpeted $840 million worth of contracts from the seminar.
